parallel.requirements: The parallel run recognized the required Node.js ESM .mjs migration, manual --a and --b parsing, Python bytes repr formatting, unsigned byte range behavior, no external npm dependencies, /output placement, and direct executable observation.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent performed initial executable probes, then assigned arg parsing, bytes repr, and struct building to three separate library-module children. After the swarm returned, the parent delegated entry-file assembly and end-to-end verification to agent-3 and then spot-checked the final output.
parallel.implementation: Children wrote /output/lib/argParser.mjs, /output/lib/pythonBytes.mjs, and /output/lib/struct.mjs using simple exported functions and number arrays. Agent-3 wrote test3.mjs with ESM imports, buildStruct, bytesRepr, RangeError handling, and an ESM main guard.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The integration child consumed the completed library modules, wrote /output/test3.mjs, and the parent later read the entry and pythonBytes files, listed /output, and ran sample commands before final response. Artifact validation copied test3.mjs and three libraries.
parallel.verification: Module children ran focused unit checks. Agent-3 ran sample diffs, edge cases, exit-code checks, forty random comparisons, and a full byte sweep. The official evaluator then completed with 126 of 126 samples passed.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished or incorrect behavior is visible at closure. All four subagents completed, the parent received their results, local checks passed, the artifact was valid, and the official evaluator passed.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same ESM .mjs migration, manual argparse behavior, construct Int8ul range behavior, Python bytes repr formatting, no external dependencies, /output placement, and use of the reference executable.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single main actor owned the complete path: executable probing, module design, library creation, entry creation, local verification, and final delivery. There were no child ownership boundaries or handoffs.
serial.implementation: The serial agent wrote pyint.mjs, pybytes.mjs, construct.mjs, argparse.mjs, and test3.mjs. It used a mini argparse and construct facade plus bytes repr formatting and wired them through the entry point.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The same actor wrote every module and the entry file, then delivered a final summary. Artifact validation copied test3.mjs plus four library modules.
serial.verification: The serial agent observed sample and edge executable outputs, checked error behavior, ran comparison loops for samples and edges, and checked usage/error exits. The official evaluator completed with 126 of 126 samples passed.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished or incorrect behavior is visible at closure. The serial run had no subagent activity, completed its local checks, produced a valid artifact, and passed the official evaluator.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the migration requirements and included them in the module and integration briefs, including ESM .mjs, manual arguments, bytes repr, range behavior, no dependencies, and executable observation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same requirements directly from the prompt and through its executable probes before writing the full solution locally.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement coverage difference affected the outcome. Parallel distributed recognized requirements across child briefs, while serial kept them in one actor.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split the task into three library-module children and a later integration child, each with a distinct file and deliverable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one actor to own probing, implementation, integration, verification, and delivery without subagents.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel created explicit ownership boundaries but they were non-overlapping and completed; serial avoided handoffs by centralizing all work.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs specified file paths, exports, argument and data contracts, and verification expectations; the integration brief restated the three library APIs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial designed its interfaces locally, using pyint, pybytes, construct, argparse, and an entry file under one continuous context.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel depended on explicit handoff contracts and child summaries; serial kept interfaces internal. The parallel contracts were sufficient and did not produce incompatibility.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel implemented parseArgs, buildStruct, bytesRepr, and a small entry file using plain arrays and ESM imports.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented a broader mini-library shape with pyint, pybytes, construct, argparse, and an entry file.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The implementation structures differed, but both encoded the same CLI behavior, Int8ul range handling, bytes repr formatting, and output placement required by the task.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children returned completed module handoffs through AgentSwarm; the parent then launched and received the integration child result before final spot-checks.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle because the only actor retained local results and proceeded sequentially to final verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had join and handoff steps that completed cleanly; serial avoided those steps. No parallel result was trapped, ignored, or left unjoined.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote separate library files under /output/lib, agent-3 read those libraries and wrote the entry file, and the parent listed and tested the final tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote all libraries and the entry file from the same actor, so there was no cross-agent shared-write surface.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used a shared workspace with disjoint file ownership and later integration; serial used a single writer. The parallel shared writes did not create a collision, overwrite, or provenance problem.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verified each module, then the integration child compared samples, edge cases, exit codes, random cases, and a full byte sweep; official evaluation passed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial verified executable behavior, samples, edge cases, error exits, and then official evaluation passed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both reached strong whole-task acceptance. Parallel verification was split across module children and the integration child; serial verification was centralized.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used four subagents and substantially more time and tokens, but did not time out and closed after local and official verification succeeded.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents, completed faster, and closed after local and official verification succeeded.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel was more expensive organizationally, while serial was shorter and centralized. The extra parallel budget use did not displace required work or create an adverse closure state.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome. The current completed official evaluations report both parallel and serial as passing 126 of 126 samples. The task-solving difference is that the parallel run distributed three library modules plus entry integration across four children and then spot-checked the integrated result, while the serial run solved the same migration in one local trajectory.
parallel_contributors: Parallel decomposition produced usable argParser, struct, pythonBytes, and entry modules with completed child handoffs and end-to-end verification.
serial_contributors: Serial centralized executable probing, module creation, entry wiring, and comparison tests in one actor and also produced a passing artifact.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel used simpler function-oriented modules and number arrays, while serial used a mini argparse/construct facade and a different module naming scheme.
Serial completed faster with fewer tokens because it avoided child setup and handoff overhead, but this did not change acceptance.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: No outcome difference; both official completed evaluations passed 126 of 126.

candidates.reason: Implementation owners existed: three children owned concrete library modules and an integration child owned the entry implementation.
The parent explicitly delegated entry integration and end-to-end verification to agent-3 after the library swarm completed.
Assembly was owned by agent-3, which wrote /output/test3.mjs, and artifact validation found the expected entry file.
The parent carried the pipeline across probing, module creation, integration, final spot-check, final response, and official pass.
The parent did initial executable probing before delegation, but that probe did not block productive work into an adverse delay or incomplete closure.
Investigation preceded implementation, but the later parallel implementation and verification completed successfully without deadline-constrained unfinished work.
No indispensable implementation, integration, or correction path was underallocated; the module and entry paths all completed and passed.
The four-agent fan-out used more budget than serial but all children completed, the run did not time out, and verification was not displaced.
Each child scope was narrow: one library module or the entry integration, and no child left indispensable assigned work unfinished.
The child briefs included the relevant task constraints, assigned file path, exported API, and verification duty; no brief omission produced unusable work or rework.
The parent specified concrete exports parseArgs, bytesRepr, buildStruct, and the integration child consumed those APIs successfully.
No known requirement, finding, checkpoint, or current-file fact disappeared between children and parent; the integration step used the returned APIs.
The swarm and integration handoffs were long but decision-usable; parent and integrator consumed them and no dependent action remained unfinished.
No child or parent acted on superseded workspace or requirement state; agent-3 read the current library files before writing the entry.
The returned child handoffs described distinct compatible modules and no unresolved incompatible report or contract blocked integration.
The parent closed after end-to-end child verification and its own spot-checks, and there was no visible unresolved integrated mismatch before closure.
No replacement or retry child was launched, so there was no repeated work caused by a missing checkpoint or inherited state.

candidates.reason: All parallel children reached completed handoffs; there is no explicit cancellation or interruption before needed work finalized.
The complete candidate was promoted and placed as /output/test3.mjs before closure, then verified; no ready deliverable was left unfinalized.
The entry file was written before integration comparisons, random sweep, and parent spot-checks; no later merge invalidated prior verification.
Delegated implementations were written to /output, returned to the parent, read by the integration child, and included in the final artifact.
The verifier-like integration child returned concrete successful sample, edge, exit-code, random, and sweep verification to the parent.
No required child failed, aborted, or was cancelled, so there was no unfinished failed scope for the parent to take over.
The parent consumed the completed swarm result by launching the integration child and consumed the integration result before final spot-checks.
The parent waited for foreground child results and the run did not time out; there was no near-deadline wait that ignored available progress.
Concurrent children wrote different files with distinct responsibilities and no overlapping behavior or competing build ownership requiring reconciliation.
No two live agents edited the same source or configuration file, and no actor had to reconcile another live same-file change.
No agent replaced, deleted, recreated, or wholesale rewrote another agent's non-entry library or configuration source.
Only the integration child owned and wrote the entry deliverable test3.mjs; no competing live owner or user of that deliverable was overwritten.
There was no broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion that replaced multiple current outputs or invalidated another agent's final-tree provenance.
Several live agents wrote under the shared /output tree, but their file scopes were disjoint and no concrete unstable-state or provenance problem resulted.
Integration intentionally consumed the assigned library outputs, not accidental temporary files, caches, fixtures, or generated artifacts as a reference environment.
